question.leadin: This province's sovereignty movement grew stronger during its "Quiet Revolution."
question.text: Name this largest Canadian province, the only majority French-speaking one.
question.clue: Paul Rose was a terrorist operating in this province and was arrested after the murder of Pierre Laporte.

swap.text: This island, discovered by Leif Eriksson, names part of a province joined with the mainland portion of Labrador.
swap.clue: Two 1948 referenda ended this territory's dominion status under Joey Smallwood and Louis St. Laurent; it had earlier rejected Confederation.

question.leadin: The sign language used by this group is considered severely endangered, with less than forty native speakers worldwide.
question.text: Name this ethnic group that is indigenous to the arctic regions of Greenland and North America. They are known for their use of kayaks and dog sleds in transportation and hunting.
question.clue: In the 1950s, this ethnic group's dogs were killed by the RCMP.

swap.leadin: This party was led by Edward Heath in the early 1970s.
swap.text: Name this party founded by Robert Peel that feuds with the Labour Party.
swap.clue: One member of this party cited an old woman who refused to lease to immigrants in his Rivers of Blood speech.

question.text: The Iroquois engaged in this series of conflicts in the seventeenth century with the Huron and the French that were named after creatures with valuable pelts.
question.clue: The Haudenosaunee fought these conflicts against the French and the Huron to gain control over the fur trade.

swap.leadin: This man's first term as Prime Minister ended following a scandal which involved bribes from the Canada Pacific Railway.
swap.text: Name this first Canadian prime minister.
swap.clue: One of his administrations fell after he was accused of corruption involving financier Hugh Allan in the Pacific Scandal, and his arrangement to purchase Rupert's Land instigated a Metis uprising.

question.leadin: Answer the following about mass hysterias in history, none of which involve Pumpkin Spice Lattes.
question.text: In 1938, unsubstantiated reports of a "slasher" paralyzed a British town of this name. Another city of this name was leveled in 1917 by a massive ship explosion and provides Boston a Christmas tree every year as thanks for its subsequent aid.
question.clue: During the French and Indian War, the British army kept prisoners on Georges Island in this city's harbor.

swap.text: This 1759 battle in Canada was a major victory for the British even though it saw the death of General James Wolfe. The French general Louis-Joseph de Montcalm also died here.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of the Plains of Abraham [accept Battle of Quebec]
swap.answer: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
swap.clue: It resulted in the death of both commanders: for the French, the Marquis de Montcalm, and for the British, James Wolfe.

question.text: He organized resistance to the Manitoba Act, which transferred Metis-populated lands from the Hudson's Bay Company to the Canadian government. For 15 points, name this leader of the Northwest Rebellion, who was hanged in 1885 for such opposition activity.
question.clue: This man's military general Gabriel Dumont was victorious at the Battle of Duck Lake, and he was forced into capture following defeat at the Battle of Batoche.

swap.text: After De Gaulle blurted out "Vive le Quebec libre!" at Montreal's Expo 67, this Nobel-winning Liberal Canadian Prime Minister responded, "Canadians do not need to be liberated."
swap.clue: This successor to Louis St. Laurent as party leader accepted the Bomarc missile program and instituted universal healthcare.

question.leadin: This man claimed to have said "fuddle duddle" when accused of mouthing profanity in the House of Commons.
question.text: Name this Canadian Prime Minister who invoked the only peacetime usage of the War Measures Act in 1970 when dealing with the October Crisis.
question.clue: When this leader was accused of mouthing profanity at opposition members, he claimed to have said "fuddle duddle," and he improved his nation's welfare system in the "Just Society" program.

swap.text: The Plan of Union agreed upon at the Congress excluded Georgia and this northern colony from the union.
swap.clue: The 1995 Peace Prize was awarded to the conferences named for this province's village of Pugwash.

question.text: This Frenchman explored the Gulf of St. Lawrence and the St. Lawrence rivers, and is credited with giving Canada its present name.
question.clue: On their second voyage, this person made contact with the residents of the village of Stadacona.

swap.text: This only female prime minister served for only five months in 1993, and was forced out when the Progressive Conservatives were soundly defeated that year. She didn't do much as Prime Minister, but Encyclopaedia Brittanica tells us she strengthened gun control laws as Attorney General.
swap.clue: , Brian Mulroney, 1993. Thus, she became the first woman to ascend to 's highest office.

question.leadin: This prime minister wrote to Rajiv Gandhi after the bombing of Air India Flight 182, prompting Gandhi to respond that he should be the one offering condolences because most of the victims were Canadians.
question.text: Name this Conservative prime minister who pushed the failed Meech Lake Accord recognizing one province as a "distinct society."
question.clue: This negotiator of the Charlottetown Accords supported the proposal of legislation that would have acknowledged Quebec as a "distinct society" within Canada in a set of agreements named for Meech Lake.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about West African art.
swap.text: Varieties of these objects from various African cultures are extremely common display items in museums. Usually made of wood or copper, they are typically made for use in religion, as opposed to theater as in the West.
swap.clue: Another of these items made of jade was found in Pacal the Great's sarcophagus.

question.text: Some Arctic Small Tool traditions developed into phases of this culture, which notably lacked bow and drill technology. This culture preceded the Thule ("TOO-lee") culture.
question.answerHtml: Dorset culture [accept Early or Middle or Late Dorset]
question.clue: X-shaped incisions on figures' heads from this culture have been linked to shamanistic travels.

swap.text: In 1953, Mowat was falsely accused of having made up the Ihalmiut by Jean Lesage. Lesage's 1960 election as premier marked the start of this historical period of secularization and welfare state formation.
swap.clue: (+) The beginning of this movement was signaled by the Union Nationale's loss in 1960 elections to the Liberal Party led by Jean Lesage.

question.text: This founder of the Parti Quebecois is considered the spiritual father of the sovereignty movement. Noted for his ubiquitous comb over, he opposed Robert Bourassa, his predecessor in the position of Quebec's premier, during the October Crisis.

swap.leadin: This man said "There's no place for the state in the bedrooms of the nation" when defending his decriminalization of homosexual acts.
swap.text: Name this Canadian Prime Minister best known for serving during the 1970 October Crisis in Quebec, during which he invoked the War Measures Act to crack down on groups like the FLQ.
swap.answer: Joseph Philippe Pierre Yves Elliott Trudeau
swap.clue: When asked how far he would go to stop terrorism, this man responded, "Just watch me."
